attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post.

semantics.note: Retrospective claim that GPT-5 expectations had not been met, that GPT-5 had been delayed, and that this matched his earlier prediction. Faithful to the statement.

contract.note: Reading 'exactly' as consistency with the earlier prediction is lenient but ordinary. The earlier prediction did include 'no GPT-5' as an outcome. Treating the mind-blowing and world-takeover lines as rhetoric is fair.

evidence.note: Fortune, Feb 2025: the GPT-5 rollout was off script, its development was lengthy, and the world was still waiting. Contemporaneous independent reporting of a delay.
Altman's Feb 12, 2025 roadmap describes GPT-5 as a future release, so it had not shipped by publication. Company disclosure; it establishes status, not the delay itself.
Marcus's March 2024 tweet confirms he predicted 'no GPT-5, or disappointing GPT-5' by end of 2024. It establishes what he predicted, not the outcome.

reviews.rationale: By Feb 2025 GPT-5 was still forthcoming (e2), and independent reporting describes a lengthy, off-script development (e1), so its promised capabilities had not been delivered. The earlier prediction (e3) anticipated no GPT-5 or a disappointing one, which is consistent with the claim under the contract's reading of 'exactly'.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his post.

semantics.note: Isolates the profitability clause and keeps 'right now'. The productivity and scaling clauses are left out, which the scope note acknowledges.

contract.note: Reading the claim as negative aggregate GenAI net income for 2024 is an ordinary reading. The industry boundary and accounting basis were not supplied by the speaker, so they shape the result.

evidence.note: Reuters reports that OpenAI lost about $5B in 2024. This covers one company and cannot establish an industry-wide aggregate.
Notes that OpenAI has not disclosed its operating expenses or how close it is to profitability. Single company, later date; not outcome evidence.

reviews.rationale: The contract requires an industry-wide GenAI net-income estimate for 2024 with matched revenue and expenses. The packet has only one developer's reported loss and a note on missing disclosures. These show strain but cannot settle the aggregate either way.

attribution.note: Marcus asserts this himself and cites his own Fortune article.

semantics.note: 'Whole field' refers back to scaling no longer bearing the fruit it once did. Diminishing returns across the field is a faithful rendering.

contract.note: Reading 'whole field' as a widespread trend among major frontier labs, and scaling as pretraining scale, is ordinary. The evaluator chose the reporting window and the measurement basis.

evidence.note: TIME, Nov 2024, relays Reuters and Bloomberg reports of diminishing returns at several leading labs. It also records Anthropic denying any deviation from scaling laws. Second-hand and contested; no comparable data.
The DeepSeek-V3 report shows strong progress but mixes architecture and training changes. It does not isolate returns to pretraining scale.

reviews.rationale: The packet has contested reporting of slowdowns at several labs, a company denial, and one technical report showing progress. None measures returns per unit of pretraining scale across developers. The evidence does not establish or refute a field-wide decline.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his post.

semantics.note: 'Most certainly wouldn't' expresses high confidence, so this is a scored forecast. The side remark on release timing is reasonably left out.

contract.note: The concrete expectations (solving hallucinations, fixing reasoning) come from the speaker's own preceding paragraph. The support bar is low but follows his framing. Treating improvement alone as no contradiction is fair.

evidence.note: The system card, Feb 27, 2025, reports a PersonQA hallucination rate of 0.19: better than the comparison models, but hallucination clearly persists. Primary company disclosure, which the contract allows.

The launch post presents GPT-4.5 as a non-reasoning model that is expected only to 'hallucinate less', with stronger reasoning still ahead. The appendix scores the drafter cites are not visible in the excerpt.

reviews.rationale: GPT-4.5 was released on Feb 27, 2025. OpenAI's own release documents show hallucinations persist (0.19 on PersonQA) and reasoning was not fixed, while noting real improvements. This meets the early-resolution rule. The model did not meet the hallucination and reasoning expectations the speaker named.
